$comment: THE MOST VALUABLE FILE IN THIS REPOSITORY. If any case fails, nothing ships (SPEC 7.5). Language-neutral on purpose: the TypeScript engine consumes it now and the Kotlin port consumes it at AN2, and a divergence on any case fails both builds (D20). Never edit an expected value to make code pass - a fixture that will not pass is a question for the operator, never a code change.
source: Worked examples published by the Administration fiscale cantonale (AFC), Geneva, for the avenant of 27 June 2023 in force 1 January 2026. VERIFIED 09.09.2026 against https://www.ge.ch/imposition-du-teletravail-personnes-frontalieres/regles-missions-temporaires-etranger (page updated 19.05.2026): all six cases exact on inputs and on all four outputs. Legal review still pending - see P1-P3 in docs/regulatory-sources.md.

commonInput.$comment: All six cases are full-time, full-year, Geneva, whole days, on the simplified 240-day basis, so totalWorkDays is 240 and fiscalCeilingDays is 96.

missionSplitNote: The published cases give a single mission total (MT). The engine takes missionDaysFrance and missionDaysThirdState separately, because France missions are imputed before third-state ones and the two are collected differently (SPEC 7.2 step 5). Every case below places the whole total in missionDaysFrance, which is the ordinary situation for a French-resident frontalier and reproduces the published Swiss/France split exactly. A case exercising the imputation ORDER is a unit test, not a fixture, since the AFC published no such example.

cases.note: Comfortably inside the ceiling. No missions, so nothing competes for the allowance and every working day is taxed in Switzerland.
cases.verified_by: transcription: Claude via ge.ch; legal review pending

cases.note: Headroom binds before the cap. 96 - 91 = 5 days of room against a 10-day cap, so only 5 of the 8 mission days can be credited and 3 are taxed in France. Lands exactly on 40.00.
cases.verified_by: transcription: Claude via ge.ch; legal review pending

cases.note: THE TRUNCATION CASE. The cap binds: 12 days of room but only 10 may be credited, so 94/240 = 39.1666... The AFC publishes 39.16, so the engine truncates to 2 dp. Rounding would give 39.17 and would not match the filing. This is also the case where the two rates differ most visibly - 39.16 declarable against 45.0 of days actually spent outside Switzerland.
cases.verified_by: transcription: Claude via ge.ch; legal review pending

cases.note: Headroom binds hard: 2 days of room, so 2 of 12 mission days are credited and 10 are taxed in France. Lands exactly on 40.00 from the other direction to case b.
cases.verified_by: transcription: Claude via ge.ch; legal review pending

cases.note: THE REGIME-LOST CASE. Telework alone (144) exceeds the ceiling (96), so the regime does not apply and mission days are EXCLUDED from the declared rate: 144/240 = 60.00, not 149/240. The missions are still taxed in France - frenchTaxedDays is 149 - which is the detail SPEC 7.2 step 5 warns is easy to get wrong. Folding them into the rate would misstate the AFC filing.
cases.verified_by: transcription: Claude via ge.ch; legal review pending

cases.note: THE SECOND TRUNCATION CASE, and missions only. No telework at all, so the full 10-day cap is creditable out of 30 mission days: 10/240 = 4.1666... The AFC publishes 4.16. Proves the truncation rule is not an artefact of case c.
cases.verified_by: transcription: Claude via ge.ch; legal review pending
